items.text: Persepolis football team, after changes in the transfer season and youth development by Mehdi Tartaar, will face Shams Azar Qazvin in the first week of the Iranian Premier League. This match marks the start of the new league season. Additionally, an interview with Mazdak Mirzaei, Mohammad Taghavi, and Raha Pourbakhsh was conducted on the Hattrick program.

A citizen in a video addressed to Mohseni Ejei and Ahmad Vahidi called for an end to warmongering. He emphasized that people have limited patience amid the livelihood crisis. This message was sent to the remaining government officials.

The Ministry of Intelligence announced the arrest of two individuals in a case related to foreign infiltration and interference. Two French embassy employees present at the detention site were interrogated by security agents. These diplomats were handed over to the French embassy after the interrogation.

Saeed Maadani cited ideological selection, limited scientific communication, brain drain, and weakened academic freedom as reasons for the decline of Iranian universities. Moloud Hajizadeh stated that after the Cultural Revolution, the educational system became increasingly closed, leading to the decline in academic standing. These remarks were made in an interview with Iran International.

Donald Trump has faced multiple assassination attempts in the past two years. One attempt involved the IRGC trying to kill him with the help of a Pakistani man. Additionally, a shooting at his campaign rally in Pennsylvania resulted in Trump being wounded in the ear.

Majidreza Khaki stated that about 700 tons of rice labeled as "American rice" have been imported into Iran through Iraq since the beginning of the year. These shipments were brought in by individuals without official registration and are not considered smuggling. There is no official plan for direct rice imports from the United States.

Retirees of the Isfahan Steel Pension Fund protested today in front of the Isfahan governor's office due to unmet demands. They demanded the establishment of basic and supplementary insurance, payment of overdue medical expenses, and implementation of the third phase of salary adjustment. The protesters also emphasized improving their living conditions.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International criticizing a government ceremony with a symbolic coffin for Ali Khamenei. He described the ceremony as "necrophilia" and protested its expenses.

Several tattoo service centers in Ardabil were closed by order of the provincial prosecutor. Several individuals related to these centers were arrested. Providing tattoo services to both women and men and sharing related images on social media were cited as reasons for the action.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, announced that metro and bus services in the capital will be free until the end of the war. He did not specify the exact time when these free services will end. This statement was made in response to journalists' questions.

Hamid Bord, Deputy Minister of Oil and CEO of the National Oil Company, denied oil release from Qeshm oil facilities. He stated that if pollution exists, its source should be investigated along the route of tankers and marine vessels. Bord identified the US as responsible for the oil stains in Qeshm.

A citizen in Al-Ghadir market square in Ahvaz criticized Masoud Pezeshkian about the darkness caused by the power outage. He mentioned disruptions in activities and jobs. This video was published on social media.

Kamran Ghazanfari, a Tehran representative, said the current problems in the country are due to wrong foreign policies and mismanagement by officials. He added that the negotiation team has adopted a weak and eager approach to negotiations. According to him, the current situation is unrelated to the war, and the best action is for the government to step aside.

Several underground and unauthorized tattoo salons in Ardabil were identified and sealed. Several people have been arrested in connection with this, and investigations to identify other accomplices continue. These centers operated by publishing images contrary to public decency.

The head of the Yazd Emergency Center stated that most emergency calls and missions are related to traffic accidents. In the first four months of this year, 83,700 calls were made to the emergency center. Over 7,300 of these calls were related to traffic accidents.

Mohammadreza Mirtajeddini stated that the decision about continuing the nightly government gatherings depends on Mojtaba Khamenei. He denied that these gatherings would end with the conclusion of the month of Safar. These gatherings will continue as long as internal and external threats exist.

Ismail Baghaei, spokesman for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that negotiations between Iran and Oman have had a positive trend despite what he called 'US obstructions.' According to him, the two sides have reached an agreement on the shipping traffic map in the Strait of Hormuz. This action was the result of cooperation among various institutions with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs at the center and the participation of defense, security, and environmental sectors.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the attack on a ship affiliated with Abu Dhabi National Oil Company in the Strait of Hormuz was carried out by the Islamic Republic. The ministry condemned the attack as hostile and called for an end to the attacks and the unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The UAE described the action as a threat to regional stability and global energy security.

Vladimir Putin traveled for the first time to the Iturup Island, a disputed area between Russia and Japan. The Japanese Prime Minister called the move unacceptable, and Japan's Foreign Ministry summoned the Russian ambassador. This trip triggered diplomatic reactions.

Jafar Pourkabegani, a member of parliament and former governor of Bushehr, is accused of involvement in the suppression and killing of protesters during the "Iranian National Revolution." This information comes from reports and data received from citizens and Iran International sources. Farzad Fattahi from Iran International has explained this issue.

Two citizens named Esmail Basar and his son Zakaria Basar were arrested by the intelligence forces in Bukan. With these arrests, the total number of detainees in recent days in this city reached eight. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Two new cases of Caspian seal deaths were recorded on the coasts of Mazandaran. The total deaths of this species since the beginning of the year have reached 25. The carcasses were too decomposed for autopsy and were buried hygienically.

Fifty Russian and Belarusian swimmers participated as neutrals in the 2026 European Swimming Championships in Saint-Denis, France. This decision followed the lifting of sanctions by the World Aquatics Federation against these athletes. Ukrainian sports officials have protested this matter.

Ali Khazarian, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, warned about the dangers of yielding on the Strait of Hormuz issue. He said that retreating in this matter would increase enemy pressure on the country. Khazarian emphasized that opening the Strait of Hormuz is interpreted as weakness and retreat.

Houshang Hasan Yari pointed out ambiguities regarding the claim of the captivity of three Su-24 pilots in Qatar. He questioned why the Islamic Republic raised the issue six months after the incident. He also warned that this claim could weaken Iran's relations with Qatar.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan expressed concern over Israel's continued attacks on Lebanon. He emphasized prioritizing the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. He also explained that the Mecca defense agreement allows for joint actions and the future inclusion of other countries.
Shakila Ghasemi, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Kerman, was released from Kerman prison on bail. This release took place on Saturday, 24th of Mordad. Harana News Agency reported this news.

Workers of Salman Farsi Petrochemical gathered today in front of the Mahshahr representative's office. They demand clarification of their employment status and protest the change from direct contracts to contractor status. These workers were previously laid off and have received a labor office ruling for reinstatement.

The Israeli Prime Minister's Office announced that Hezbollah violated the ceasefire in Lebanon by attacking Israeli forces in a security zone. Three Israeli soldiers were seriously injured in the attack. In response, the Israeli army targeted Hezbollah's command headquarters.

Mahtab Gholizadeh stated that installment buying has expanded in Iran due to the worsening livelihood crisis. This type of purchase now includes items like meat, chicken, and medical services. This situation indicates a decline in purchasing power turning into a serious crisis.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that after the killing of a senior Hezbollah commander in an Israeli attack on southern Beirut, Iran's negotiations with the US were halted. He said that following this attack, Iran threatened a strong response and rejected Trump's tweet about lifting the siege and opening the Strait of Hormuz. These events highlight the intensity and complexity of the negotiations.

The head of the government in Iran described recent price increases and their impact on citizens' livelihoods as natural, citing economic blockade and US oil sanctions as reasons. He mentioned that oil revenues have decreased and import routes have become longer. The continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz has also increased pressure on Iran's economy.

Mohammad Bagherzadeh announced that three army pilots whose fighters crashed in Esfand are alive and detained by Qatari forces. These three pilots have been in detention for about six months, and the Qatari government has not allowed them to meet or contact their families. Previously, the status of these pilots was unclear.

The Israeli army announced that Ali Samir Al-Hajj Hassan, a commander of a Hezbollah unit in southern Lebanon, was killed. The attack was in response to Hezbollah's actions against Israeli forces in the security buffer zone. Several other Hezbollah members were also killed in the attack.

Masoud Farhikhteh, a teachers' union activist, has been deprived of visits and phone contact with his family for 53 days. After spending 20 days in solitary confinement, he is now held in a separate room as punishment. These measures followed his release of statements regarding prisoners' demands.

Saeid Mollaei, former Iranian national judo player, traveled to Israel for a friendly match with the Israeli judo champion. He said freedom is near and a victory celebration will soon be held in Tehran. This is Mollaei's fourth trip to Israel.

Iran International has identified 9 members of the Ministry of Intelligence corruption network known as the Shayan network. This network has failed to return about two thousand trillion tomans of oil money. Members include the son of Mohsen Rezaee, the son of Fallahian, the Minister of Intelligence under Hashemi, and the son-in-law of the Minister of Intelligence under Rouhani.

Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel, condemned Hezbollah's attack on Israeli forces and the violation of the ceasefire. He stated that Hezbollah knowingly injures Israeli soldiers expecting a response. Huckabee also claimed that Hezbollah gathers children and moves them to military zones to put them at risk.

The first week of the Iranian Premier League started with victories for Esteghlal, Tractor, and Sepahan. Esteghlal defeated Mes Shahr-e Babak 4-0. Tractor and Sepahan also won 2-0 against Paykan and Chadormalu respectively.

The Deputy Minister of Oil denied any connection between the oil patches in the Persian Gulf and the Qeshm oil facilities. The probable source of pollution is the route of oil tankers and vessels. The exact source of pollution and environmental damage extent remain unknown.

The Central Bank announced that a foreign provider has revoked the security certificates of some websites related to the bank. Users may receive security error messages when accessing these sites. This issue is not due to a cyberattack, and necessary measures to resolve the problem are underway.

Seyed Javad Mousavi, detained in connection with the December 2025 protests, was transferred to Birjand prison. He was sentenced to five years in prison. His transfer took place today, Saturday, August 14.

An audio file from a secret meeting of the Media and Cyberspace Headquarters in Pakdasht reveals concerns of Basij and IRGC-affiliated institutions about a new wave of public protests and infiltration into security agencies. The meeting was held following incidents including the death of Hamidreza Rajabzadeh. The Media and Cyberspace Headquarters operates under the IRGC.

Reza Sepahvand, spokesperson for the Energy Commission of the Parliament, stated that gasoline imports have stopped due to a maritime blockade. He mentioned supply problems considering the number of vehicles. He also emphasized that decisions about gasoline should consider the economic capacity of the people and existing capacities.

The Israeli army announced that last night it targeted Hezbollah's infrastructure in southern Lebanon in response to Hezbollah's operations. The Lebanese president said these attacks aimed to disrupt peace talks. The report is by Ashkan Safaei, a journalist from Iran International.

Peyvand and Borna Naeimi, two Baha'i citizens, have been held in Kerman prison for over seven and five months respectively without a clear decision. No judicial ruling has been made regarding their status. This has been confirmed by a source close to their families.

Ramin Kashif Azar, CEO of Imam Khomeini Airport City Company, stated that the air transport industry was completely halted during the war and airlines were in a worse condition than other sectors. He added that problems caused by the war still persist and efforts have been made to avoid layoffs and ensure employees receive their salaries.

The official Yemeni government stated that the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at Al-Mokha port on Friday, August 14, killing at least four civilians. A video showed boats catching fire and damage to port facilities. The Houthis confirmed targeting a military gathering of forces supported by Saudi Arabia.

Peyman Hadadi announced negotiations with Ramin Rezaeian, Mohammad Javad Hosseinnejad, and Kasra Taheri. Rezaeian was interested in returning to Persepolis but his requested amount exceeded the club's budget. The club also could not pay the requested amounts for Hosseinnejad and Taheri, and eventually Taheri was signed through Shahrabadi.

An audio file from a media and cyberspace headquarters meeting in Pakdasht shows officials expressing concern about the potential resurgence of protests and security system breaches. Jamshid Barzegar stated that the Islamic Republic is trying to justify harsher crackdowns by portraying threats to Basij forces. He added that people have so far shown restraint against the violence of suppressive forces.

Due to lack of workplace safety, eight workers in Tabriz, Mashhad, Mahabad, and Bandar Abbas were involved in accidents. Seven were injured and one worker died. Three of the injured were firefighters.

Persepolis football team defeated Shams Azar 2-0 in the first week of the Iranian Premier League. The goals were scored by Mohammad Mahdi Mohibi and Mohammad Omri. Also, the match between Zob Ahan and Foolad Khuzestan ended in a goalless draw.
The 60-day ceasefire period has ended. Washington is on the verge of unprecedented economic pressure against Tehran. This was discussed in the audio version of Titrawal with Niusha Saremi.
A group of contract workers employed in the Green Belt project of Ahvaz Municipality reported three months of unpaid wages.

Moroccan security forces dispersed migrants attempting to enter Ceuta from Fnideq on Saturday, August 15. Security measures were increased following social media messages calling for mass crossing. Rabat has warned that organizers of this call will face legal action.

The Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson firmly denied the claims of Iranian pilots' detention. Qatar stated that it took necessary defensive actions after the airspace violation. Coordination has also been made for the delivery of one pilot's body.

At least six protests were held today, Saturday, 24 Mordad, in Tehran, Isfahan, Mahshahr, Sirjan, and Zirab. Participants included families of cystic fibrosis patients, retired steel and mining workers, petrochemical and municipal workers, and land applicants. They demanded attention to their demands.

Due to rising prices and the livelihood crisis in Iran, 5 and 10 kilogram rice packages are being sold in installments at Etka chain stores. These stores are affiliated with the Ministry of Defense of the Islamic Republic. Previous reports also indicated that citizens have been forced to buy goods in installments due to low purchasing power.

A program titled 'Outlook' with Mehdi Mahdavi Azad discusses the unprecedented economic war declared by the US against Iran. The full version of this program is available on YouTube. The program addresses economic developments between Iran and the US.

Fatemeh Tadrisi, a political prisoner, was granted leave from Kachouyi Prison in Karaj. This leave was granted on the morning of Saturday, 24 Mordad, due to the death of her husband. The news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad warned about the reduction of essential goods reserves and the risk of famine in Iran. He said that increased US pressure could lead Iran into a full-scale economic war. This situation may deepen the economic crisis.

Kaveh Yaghmaei explained that his new piece musically narrates recent events and the immortal figures of the national revolution. The work features the Lion and Sun flag and an image of Reza Pahlavi. He emphasized that the future system should be determined by the choice of the Iranian people.

Shayan Samiei said that closing the Strait of Hormuz harms the Islamic Republic the most and increases the cost of imports and economic pressure on the Iranian people. He added that the Islamic Republic has no clear plan for the Strait of Hormuz and the idea of exclusive ownership of this waterway is not compatible with geographical reality. Samiei also stated that the Islamic Republic tries to institutionalize this illusion in the minds of the Iranian people and the global public opinion.
Mehregan Namavar, a poet from Dehdasht, was transferred to Yasuj prison on July 4, 2026. She is serving her prison sentence there. This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Amir Aliakbari was knocked out in the first round of the main ACA event fight in Moscow by Alihan Vakhayev. This loss ended his chance to continue the championship path and win the heavyweight belt. After the fight, Aliakbari said, "Tonight was not my night."

Mostafa Nakhaei, the representative of Nehbandan, stated that part of the daily 20 million liters of fuel smuggling is authorized and occurs at the border. He emphasized that smuggling is not limited to hidden smugglers. These remarks were in response to fuel smuggling statistics.

Donald Trump shared a video of Behnam Ben Taleblu, Senior Director of Iran Program at Foundation for Defense of Democracies, on Truth Social. Ben Taleblu argued that combining financial pressure with a US blockade could intensify damage to Tehran's military capability and economy. He said intensified pressure could maximize the damage from previous military actions and would be effective.

Peyman Hadadi, CEO of Persepolis, commented on Sepahan and Tractor's proposal for a three-team tournament, stating Persepolis had a chance to win last season. He added that if a five-team tournament is held, Persepolis can participate.

Ebrahim Rezaei criticized the performance of the Islamic Republic's diplomacy, stating that its weakness has allowed Turkey and Pakistan to benefit from Iran's military actions in the region. He added that if diplomacy were strong, Iran would be the one benefiting regionally. Rezaei emphasized that Iranian fighters have done the hard work, but others are reaping the benefits.

Davood Rangi, an import official at the Chamber of Commerce, warned that the blockade of ports could lead to food shortages. Food reserves are sufficient for only three to four months. Land routes and northern ports cannot replace the import of 23 million tons of goods from southern ports.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the Parliament, commented on the US president in a tweet. He said the US president should worry about his own security instead of boasting about the Strait of Hormuz. Azizi warned that the US president might end up hiding in a food truck.

Morad Veisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, stated that the increase in gasoline prices and removal of quotas could cause dissatisfaction among millions of passenger drivers. Gasoline prices may rise to 87,000 tomans per liter, starting from Kerman. This issue could lead to widespread protests by drivers.

Reza Dalman, a protesting student at Sharif University, was expelled for symbolically hanging a mouse's body from a tree. This action was taken by university officials and the Ministry of Science under the Medicalian government. The incident led to the widespread use of the term 'Moushali' among protesters.

The president of Qatar's Football Federation wrote to the AFC president stating that he was not consulted before the open letter by three confederations against the FIFA president was published. Infantino faces opposition from UEFA, AFC, and CONCACAF. The Qatar Football Federation president requested an explanation from the AFC about consultations before releasing the statement.

Brad Cooper, the commander of CENTCOM, concluded his 10-day trip to the Middle East. During the trip, he visited six countries and an aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea and met with senior officials. Cooper described the mission of the USS Abraham Lincoln as one of the most important operational missions.

Despite the announced agreement between Iran and Oman on the shipping traffic map in the Strait of Hormuz, disagreements over its implementation continue and no joint statement has been issued. The US has emphasized continuing the naval blockade of Iran and announced new sanctions and economic pressures. This report was prepared by Marzieh Hosseini from Iran International.

Reza Alijani said the "Women, Life, Freedom" movement caused less polarization in society compared to the protests of December 2025. He added that polarization can give the Islamic Republic's security forces an excuse for more repression. Alijani attributed this polarization to some misguided and unaware opposition groups.

The audio version of the program 'Politics' with Murad Vaisi has been released. This episode discusses signs of food reserve shortages in the country. The program examines the status of food reserves.

Turkish media have focused on the consequences of five years of Taliban rule in Kabul on the fifth anniversary of the city's fall. The situation of Afghan women and girls, including restrictions on education, employment, and social participation, has been a key focus. The report was prepared by Farzia Sabti from Iran International.

Amirhossein Sabeti, a member of parliament, stated that the Arab countries in the Persian Gulf hosting US military bases should be targeted for revenge. He claimed these countries were involved in the assassination attempt on Khamenei. He also said some senior officials apologized to the Arab countries for the US bases being targeted.

Five years after the Taliban's return to power, Afghanistan's administrative structure has undergone significant changes. Skilled personnel have left the administrations and women have been excluded. Additionally, graduates of religious schools have widely entered the government.

A group of Iranians living in Brisbane, Australia, held a protest on Saturday against executions in Iran. Participants demanded the halt of death sentences and the release of political prisoners. The protest was organized by the group "Iran Tomorrow - Responsibility Today."

The Israeli army displayed a collection of weapons seized from Hamas and Hezbollah. These weapons include mortars, cannons, sniper rifles, and anti-tank launchers made in Iran, as well as equipment from Russia and China. A German-made MG-34 machine gun was also seized from a Hezbollah base.

Mike Pompeo, former US Secretary of State, warned that withdrawing from the conflict with the Islamic Republic without victory could undermine Washington's allies' trust. He opposed ending the conflict, stating it would not be seen as a victory. Pompeo emphasized that Washington should continue its operations until the defeat of the Islamic Republic.

Hossein Shariatmadari called on officials to enforce the hijab law. He condemned the lack of action against unveiled women, calling it religiously and politically forbidden. Shariatmadari also stated that intelligence agencies opposing the Islamic Republic support the unveiling.

The Judiciary News Agency reported the execution of Shahram Sadeghi, a December protester in Karaj, on charges of operational actions benefiting Israel and the US. He was arrested for running over officers with a vehicle on January 8. The execution was carried out on charges against national security and interests.

The Israeli army attacked Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon. The Israeli defense minister stated that no score on any front will remain unsettled. This attack was in response to Hezbollah's actions against Israeli forces.

Ali Nahavandi, head of the Islamic Research Center of the Parliament, stated that the US, Israel, and their regional allies should know that no hostile action will go unanswered. He emphasized that deterrence is not just a threat of response but creating a calculation where refraining from war is more rational for the enemy.

Rahmatollah Norouzi, representative of Aliabad Katoul, reported very high housing inflation and serious pressure on buying and renting in large and small cities. He stated that single and married young people face serious difficulties in securing deposits, rent, and purchasing housing.

The execution of Shahram Sadeghi, a protester from the December uprising, was carried out on the morning of August 16. He was sentenced to death for operational actions in favor of Israel, the US, and hostile groups. After interrogation, Sadeghi admitted to driving the car towards officers and setting it on fire.

Ali Emami Rad stated that there should be no negotiations with the US and that the military doctrine should shift from defensive to offensive. He emphasized Iran's deep enmity with the US and Israel and vowed not to relent until the avengers of the martyred leader are punished. He also highlighted the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz as a paternal heritage and key to global power.

The spokesperson of Iran's Foreign Ministry announced an agreement between Tehran and Muscat on a shipping map in the Strait of Hormuz. This agreement follows diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume normal ship traffic. More details were provided by an Iran International reporter.

Omid Memarian commented on the fate of four missing pilots, stating that the Islamic Republic claims three pilots are in Qatar. Qatari officials have denied this claim. The Islamic Republic must provide evidence of their survival and location.

Reza Goharzad reported the continuation of the maritime blockade of Iranian ports and fuel distribution problems. He mentioned long gasoline queues and the emergence of a black market. He also said that gasoline imports do not solve price and distribution issues and dissatisfaction could lead to street protests.

The Israeli army announced that Abu Hasan Alla, a senior commander of the Badr unit of Hezbollah, was killed. This action was in response to Hezbollah's attacks on Israeli forces in the security zone. Hasan Alla was involved in multiple attacks, including launching explosive drones.

Hamshahri newspaper criticized mixed-gender sports and optional dress codes in parks. It referred to videos from Tehran, Qom, and Mashhad showing boys and girls exercising together. Hamshahri called for more cultural awareness and supervision of sports programs.

Abbas Goudarzi announced that the government has one and a half months from August 20 to introduce the proposed ministers of intelligence and defense to the parliament. There is an idea that the requirement of Ijtihad for the intelligence minister may not be necessary. This issue requires legal amendment, and the government must submit a bill to the parliament.

Ahmad Alavi stated that due to international consensus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and China's losses from its closure, the US may increase pressure on buyers of Iranian oil. He added that the US is prepared to bear the costs of higher oil prices to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The Israeli army announced that Abu Hasan Alaa, a senior Hezbollah commander, was killed in an attack on Deir al-Zahrani. A Middle East history researcher said Hezbollah is not satisfied with the Lebanese government's treaty with Israel. The ceasefire negotiations are very fragile.

Esmaeil Faraji, deputy operations of the Basij organization, announced extensive plans to organize volunteers of the Jan-Fada system. The goal is to train and prepare these volunteers to defend the land of Iran. Additionally, the Basij combat organization has multiplied due to increased registrations.

Political and sanction pressures from Europe against the Islamic Republic are increasing. More countries outside the European Union are aligning their positions with Brussels' policies. This trend indicates an expansion of sanctions and pressures against Tehran.

The executive deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian stated that using VPNs has made enemy infiltration easier. About 75% of people oppose the use of VPNs. The sale of VPNs generates between 7 to 12 trillion tomans in revenue, but it is unclear who benefits from it.

The commander of the Missing Persons Search Committee stated that an air force expert team has been waiting for months to enter Qatar to investigate the status of three Iranian pilots. According to him, Qatari officials have obstructed the return of these pilots. The Qatari Foreign Ministry has denied these reports.

Shahram Sadeghi, a detainee from the December 2025 protests in Karaj, was executed early this morning. He was convicted of operational actions in favor of Israel, the USA, and hostile countries against national security and interests. This sentence was issued by the Revolutionary Court of Karaj.

Mehdi Eghraryan said the mayor's promise to reduce housing prices has not been fulfilled, and people have been burdened by rising prices. He criticized construction in military barracks acquired by the municipality and called for the barracks to remain in their current use. Eghraryan stated that if warnings are ignored, he will initiate a question plan against the mayor.

Dariush Rahimi, a resident of Sanandaj, was arrested by security forces at his home on Saturday, August 15. The arrest was made without a judicial warrant and involved violence. His and his wife's mobile phones were also confiscated.

Mehr News Agency warned about humorous videos of eulogies on social media. The agency emphasized that eulogies are not compatible with frivolity and blogging, and joking about them breaks cultural boundaries. It also stressed that the line between respect for sacred matters and exploitation should not be blurred.
Ali Imani Motlagh, a teacher in Lorestan province, was dismissed from his job by the disciplinary board of the provincial education department.

The police chief of Galikesh announced the closure of five women's hair salons and the arrest of their operators. The reason given was the publication of immoral images on social media. This incident took place in Galikesh county.

Hamid Hosseini, an energy expert, stated that the recent war caused damage to some facilities and made the Black Sea unsafe. These developments have created serious challenges for gasoline supply. Regional changes have also affected gasoline imports.

Keyvan Ahmadi, a protest singer from Nurabad Mamasani, performed the Bakhtiari Lori song "Mar Jangeh, Mar Jangeh, Khoda Dooneh Jang Tefangeh" in front of a group of locals. He had previously been arrested for supporting the Iranian National Revolution. This performance took place in Nurabad Mamasani.

A group of Iranians living in London displayed images of the martyrs of the December protests on a truck. They held a car rally while carrying Lion and Sun flags to honor the deceased. The event took place on Saturday, August 15.

A citizen in Tehran reported that during the peak heat and after returning from work, the electricity was cut off for the third time in one day. The video highlights electricity supply issues in Tehran. Power outages during hot days have caused concerns.

A group of Social Security retirees from Shush, Karkheh, and Haft-Tappeh held a protest in front of the Social Security building in Shush today. They demanded the implementation of the equalization plan, salary increases according to inflation, and attention to their medical and livelihood problems. The protest took place on August 16.

The Judiciary news agency reported the execution of Shahram Sadeghi, a detained protester during the Iranian National Revolution in Karaj. His charges were announced as acting against national security and interests and attacking officers. Hassan Naeb Hashem provided explanations about stopping the execution cycle.

Alireza Raeisi, Deputy Minister of Health, stated that young people need jobs, housing, economic security, and a predictable future to have children. He emphasized that population growth cannot be forced. These remarks were made in the context of population increase policies.

Amir Hatami announced that any Iranian who captures or kills an American soldier will receive a $30,000 reward. Previously, plans for rewards for killing Donald Trump had also been proposed. These statements were made during a ceremony on Journalists' Day.
Masoud Alani Kohneh Qaleh was arrested by security forces in Oshnavieh. He was transferred to an unknown location by the Intelligence Department agents. This event took place yesterday.

Sattar Hashemi, the Minister of Communications, stated that the internet outage until mid-May caused over 67 trillion tomans in direct damage to the ICT sector and digital economy. He added that this figure does not include indirect costs such as lost investment opportunities and reduced business activities. Additionally, some of the damages are not financially compensable.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin pointed to contradictions in the positions of Hezbollah and the Lebanese government. Hezbollah calls for a return to agreements and Resolution 1701. However, it does not speak about disarmament and handing over weapons to the Lebanese army.
A citizen in Tehran was arrested for creating an unauthorized communication platform and transmitting classified information using Starlink satellite internet, according to the intelligence police.

Shakiba from Tehran stated that her doctor dismissed her due to the events of Dey month. She expressed regret and said she felt ashamed of her father who raised her with labor money. This issue was directly raised by Shakiba.

The representative of Hormozgan in the parliament reported low education quality and insufficient infrastructure in the province. She pointed to unequal distribution of educational resources and the impact of war on students' educational opportunities. She also called for the deployment of psychological teams to support affected students.
